chunks: Ma'ani al-Akhbar: My father, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Zurara who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Hunafa for Allah, not associating with Him.' I said: What is the Hanifiyya? He said: The Fitra.

key_terms.الْحَنِيفِيَّةُ: The state or quality of being Hanif, defined here as innate monotheism.
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةُ: The innate natural disposition or instinct with which humans are created, inclined towards recognizing God.
key_terms.حُنَفَاءَ: Plural of Hanif, referring to those who are pure in monotheism and follow the natural disposition.

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Hanifiyya according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Zurara asks Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to explain the term 'Hanifiyya' found in the Quranic verse (22:31). The Imam defines it as 'Fitra', indicating that true monotheism and pure submission to God are innate to human nature. This definition underscores the Shia theological view that the primordial disposition towards Tawhid is an inherent, uncorrupted aspect of the human soul, distinct from acquired beliefs.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/379] Ma’ani al-Akhbar: My father from Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhayna from Zurara who said:
I asked Aba Ja’far عليه السلام about the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: “Hunafa for Allah, not associating with Him (anything)” [22:31]. I said: What is the Hanifiyya? He said: The Fitra.
